newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen stocks close lower on crackdown talk.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stocks close lower on crackdown talk.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B shares ended down sharply on Wednesday as investors sold on expectations the government will soon clamp down on China's stock markets, analysts said.
The foreign currency B share index plunged 7.62 points or 4.27 percent to 170.74 on turnover of HK$130.7 million, against Tuesday's HK$137.8 million.
The domestic currency A index lost 31.49 points or 5.92 percent to close at 500.03 on turnover of 12.78 billion yuan, compared with Tuesday's 16.3 billion.
"People are expecting a real clampdown, something that really hurts, not just a warning," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Rumours swirled through China's stock markets that the authorities may suspend the trading licenses of several major brokerages for alleged market manipulation, analysts said.
"This (suspension of licenses) would immobilise the big fish and dry up the pool of funds," the Guotai analyst said.
A Hong Kong newspaper on Tuesday reported Chinese authorities have said they will no longer tolerate the recent "crazy" market gains and will soon announce clampdown measures.
Officials at the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the country's market watchdog, declined to comment on the rumours.
The government is also rumoured to be considering extending Shenzhen's transaction settlement period to three days to reduce market volatility, traders said.
This compares with the current settlement period of one day for A shares and immediate settlement for B shares, they said.
A trader at a western investment bank said an extension of the settlement period would drive investors out of the market.
Brokers also said there were rumors of top-level personnel changes in government securities departments, but officials declined to comment.
The A and B share indices are likely to fall further in the present, uncertain climate but will rebound once the government's intentions become more clear, analysts said.
"Investors are digesting the rumours now and will be quite prepared if they come true," the Guotai analyst said.
Analysts have lowered their expectations for Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd's 2553.SZ 100 million B shares debut on Thursday amid the selling trend.
"Sanonda is coming in when investors are pulling out," the Guotai analyst said.
Sanonda's foreign currency B shares will likely stay around HK$4.0, a rise of around 15 percent from the issue price of HK$3.48, analysts said.
Shenzhen Fangda Industrial Co Ltd was the worst performer in the B share market, plunging HK$1.28 or 9.70 percent to HK$11.91.
Chiwan Wharf Holdings Ltd, which on Wednesday said it would build a cargo warehouse with a Hong Kong company, bucked the market trend to rise HK$0.02 or 0.38 percent to HK$5.32.
